methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots capability-building outside major tech hubs, signaling potential for peer-to-peer distributed learning that could bridge the technology gap through community-driven education rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA institutionalizes deep AI capability development in the Richmond metro area, reinforcing concentration of expertise in the state capital while the 'community impact' framing suggests awareness of but not yet solution to distribution challenges.

signals.title: Griffith Announces $97,472 ARC Grant for AI Study in the Ninth District - Patriot Publishing LLC
signals.signal_reading: A $97,472 ARC grant specifically targeting AI study in Virginia's Ninth District (Appalachian Southwest) signals intentional investment in distributed capability-building in the state's most economically challenged region, though modest funding suggests shallow initial penetration.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Children's National and Virginia Tech collaboration creates a specialized pediatric AI innovation hub connecting NoVA healthcare infrastructure with New River Valley academic research, deepening expertise in two metros while the narrow vertical focus limits broad workforce distribution.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., Meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI Help Assistant - DVIDS
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying an AI help assistant named Amelia represents platform-delivered AI creating operational efficiency without requiring deep technical capability from end users, exemplifying shallow but functional adoption in defense-industrial contexts.
